options.text: The Hispanic share of the population nearly tripled between 1980 and 2020

options.misconception: The share rose at every census shown, from 12.5 percent in 2000 to 18.7 percent in 2020.
options.text: The Hispanic share of the population fell after 2000 and kept falling

options.misconception: At 18.7 percent, Hispanics were less than a fifth of the population, not a majority.
options.text: Hispanics were a majority of the population by 2020

options.misconception: The share rose from 16.3 percent in 2010 to 18.7 percent in 2020.
options.text: The Hispanic population stopped growing after 2010

rationales.A: The share rises from 6.4 percent to 18.7 percent, which is just under three times the 1980 figure. The table shows steady growth at every census.
rationales.B: The column rises at every step; nothing in it falls after 2000.
rationales.C: A share of 18.7 percent is well short of a majority.
rationales.D: The 2010 to 2020 step is still upward, from 16.3 to 18.7 percent.
rationales.general:
1. Read the column: 6.4, 9.0, 12.5, 16.3, then 18.7 percent.
2. Compare the ends. 18.7 is just under three times 6.4, so the share nearly tripled.
3. Check the wrong readings. Nothing falls, no figure passes 50 percent, and growth never stops.
4. The steady rise at every census is the pattern the table shows.
Remember: compare the first and last numbers before you judge how big a change is.
